title: Degree-zero Picard point injectivity and torsion lifting under field extension
statement: Let $k\subseteq k'$ be algebraically closed fields [def-sc-field-extension], and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a proper smooth connected curve [def-sc-curves]. Write $X'=X\times_k k'$ and $f':X'\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-base-change]. Let $G\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ and $G'\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}(X')$ be subgroups whose underlying sets are the degree-zero Picard classes [def-sc-pic0]. Let $j:G\to G'$ be a homomorphism whose underlying Picard classes are the canonical pullbacks. For a natural number $n$ nonzero in $k$, $j$ is injective and every $y\in G'$ with $y^n=1$ is $j(x)$ for some $x\in G$ with $x^n=1$.

source.place: Proper-case Kummer naturality sentence and affine-case Picard-torsion paragraph

proof.text: The comparison theorem identifies both degree-zero Picard subgroup models with rational points of one Jacobian and identifies j with extension of points.
Residue-field injectivity for Spec maps proves j is injective after applying the equivalence to the Jacobian points.

For nonzero n, the abelian-variety estimate gives a bijection on n-torsion points of the finite étale kernel. The kernel universal property transports a lifted point back to a Picard class, and the comparison square gives j x = y.

theorem picZero_torsion_base_change
    {k k' : Type u} [Field k] [Field k'] [IsAlgClosed k] [IsAlgClosed k'] [Algebra k k']
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] [IsProper f]
    (G : Subgroup X.Pic) (hG : (G : Set X.Pic) = f.picZero)
    (G' : Subgroup (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))).Pic)
    (hG' : (G' : Set (pullback f
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))).Pic) =
      (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))).picZero)
    (j : G →* G')
    (hj : ∀ L : G, (j L).val = Scheme.Pic.mapHom
      (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))) L.val)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : (n : k) ≠ 0) :
    Function.Injective j ∧ ∀ y : G', y ^ n = 1 → ∃ x : G, x ^ n = 1 ∧ j x = y
